Do not integrate P1. It goes back to agent-a (the record calls this REJECT). The hand-off contradicts itself. It says `status: DONE`, `integration_ready: true` and "all order tests pass". But its only evidence, E1 (`npm test -- test/orders`), exited with code 1: "5 passed, 1 failed: rejects zero quantity". The failing test is the exact behaviour REQ-7 asks for. Separately, `src/orders/billing.js:9-13` in this workspace has no quantity check: `priceOrder` still multiplies `line.price * line.quantity` without validating anything. So the changed file the hand-off describes is not in this workspace either.

**Why it matters**
If it's integrated, the lead puts a known REQ-7 failure on the integrated head, and P3 reviews a package whose own evidence already fails. Rejecting it counts as one rework cycle against P1. P2 doesn't depend on P1 and isn't affected.

**Do this first**

2. Once you have a Bash-capable session, run `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py handoff .alchemy/runs/r1/handoff-P1.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --root .` on this hand-off and on attempt 2.

- **The SHA-256 of `src/orders/billing.js`:** not computed. I can't confirm the `CLAIM_CONTRADICTS_WORKSPACE` code by digest, only by reading the file. To close it, run `Get-FileHash src/orders/billing.js -Algorithm SHA256`.
- **Whether commits `b6e8d7f` and `e41c09a` exist:** not checked. The workspace is not a git repository, so `STALE_BASE` can't be evaluated here, and the gate's committed-clean-head check will fail until it is one. To close it, run `git init`, or point `--root` at agent-a's workspace.
- **The test file:** there is no `test/orders/` directory in this workspace, so E1 can't be reproduced here. To close it, run `npm test -- test/orders` in agent-a's workspace.
